faq.q: What is a full day bottom fishing charter in Marbella?
faq.a: A full day bottom fishing charter is an 8-hour trip where you fish on the seabed for species like sea bass, grouper, and bream. Departing from Puerto Banús, you'll head 3–8 NM offshore to reefs and sandy bottoms. The boat anchors or drifts, and you use weighted rigs with bait to tempt bottom-dwelling fish. All gear, bait, and a licensed skipper are included.

faq.q: What fish can I catch on a bottom fishing charter in Marbella?
faq.a: Common catches include European sea bass (up to 10 kg), common bream, red snapper, grouper, and mackerel. In summer, you may also hook dentex or amberjack. The Mediterranean seabed around Marbella holds rocky reefs and sandy flats where these species feed. Catches vary with season and tide, but bottom fishing consistently yields good results, especially from June to October.

faq.q: How much does a full day bottom fishing charter cost in Marbella?

faq.q: What is included in the full day bottom fishing charter?

Fishing gear — rods, reels, line, hooks, sinkers, and bait — is provided at no extra cost. You just bring sunscreen, a hat, and a cooler for any fish you keep.

faq.q: Do I need a fishing license for a full day charter?
faq.a: No, you do not need a personal fishing license. The charter boat operates under a commercial fishing permit held by the skipper. You can fish legally as a guest on board. However, any fish you keep must comply with local size and bag limits, which the skipper will explain.

faq.q: Can I keep the fish I catch?

The skipper will help you measure and handle the catch. We encourage catch-and-release for smaller or protected species to sustain local stocks.

Spring and autumn also offer good fishing, but winter can be windier. Early morning departures (8:00–9:00) often yield the best catches before the sea breeze picks up.

data.body_html:
If you want to spend a full day on the Mediterranean targeting sea bass, grouper, and bream, a full day bottom fishing charter Marbella is the most direct way to do it. Departing from Puerto Banús, you'll head offshore to rocky reefs and sandy flats where bottom-dwelling fish feed. All gear, bait, drinks, and a licensed skipper are included, so you just show up and fish. Prices start at €2,299 for 8 hours on boats like the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, with larger vessels available for groups up to 12.

Why Choose a Full Day Bottom Fishing Charter in Marbella

Bottom fishing is one of the most reliable techniques in the Mediterranean. You drop a weighted rig with bait to the seabed and wait for species that live near the bottom. Unlike trolling or lure fishing, bottom fishing works in calm or choppy conditions and doesn't require high-speed boat handling. It's ideal for families, groups, or anglers who want a relaxed day on the water with a good chance of catching dinner. The waters off Marbella, from Cabopino to Estepona, hold rocky outcrops and sandy patches that attract sea bass, bream, and grouper year-round.

What You’ll Catch: Species and Seasons

The Mediterranean seabed around Marbella is home to several prized table fish. Your catch will depend on the month, but here's what to expect:

  • European sea bass (up to 10 kg) – best from May to October.
  • Common bream – abundant all year, especially near rocky bottoms.
  • Red snapper – found in deeper water (20–50 m), common in summer.
  • Grouper – larger specimens near reefs; catch-and-release encouraged.
  • Mackerel – often caught as bycatch; great for bait or eating fresh.
  • Dentex and amberjack – occasional summer visitors for experienced anglers.

Water temperatures in June–October range from 18°C to 24°C, which brings more species closer to shore. In winter, sea bass and bream remain active, but you'll need to fish deeper (30–50 m).

Fishing gear (rods, reels, bait) is provided at no extra cost.

What to Expect on the Day

Your charter departs from Puerto Banús, usually between 8:00 and 9:00 AM. The skipper will take you 3–8 nautical miles offshore to spots marked on GPS from years of experience. You'll anchor or drift over rocky reefs or sandy bottoms. The skipper sets up the rods with weighted rigs and bait (squid, sardines, or worms). You just drop the line and wait for a bite. The boat is equipped with a fish finder to locate schools, so you're not fishing blind. Lunch is served on board: light snacks, drinks, and you can even grill your catch if you keep it. The trip ends around 5:00 PM back at Puerto Banús.

Tips for a Successful Full Day Bottom Fishing Charter

  • Book your full day bottom fishing charter Marbella from June to October for the best variety.
  • Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light jacket – sea breezes can cool things down.
  • Arrive 15 minutes early at Puerto Banús for a briefing on safety and gear.
  • If you want to keep fish, bring a cooler with ice; the skipper can clean your catch.
  • Let the skipper know your experience level – they'll adjust the rigs and depth accordingly.

Catch-and-Release and Sustainability

We encourage catch-and-release for undersized or protected species, such as grouper under 5 kg or any fish that looks rare. The Mediterranean ecosystem is fragile, and responsible fishing helps keep stocks healthy. The skipper will show you how to handle fish with wet hands to protect their slime coat and release them quickly. Legal-sized sea bass, bream, and mackerel can be kept for dinner – a fresh fish grilled on the boat is hard to beat.
